solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turning on water supply, likely to bottle it, being mature

indicators.note: turning signals that the little word on is flipped round

parts.note: a spring is a natural source of water
to bottle it is British slang for losing your nerve, so someone likely to do so is chicken, a coward

explanation.surface: Someone turning on the tap is warned the water could be bottled once it has matured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' flips ON to NO. 'Bottle it' is British slang for losing your nerve at the critical moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no spring chicken is an idiom saying they are no longer young, i.e. getting on in years.

clue.text: Remedy in no way unusual

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way
rum is British informal for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A cure described as perfectly ordinary in every respect.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM, meaning strange, is chiefly British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack medicine or pet cure, a supposed remedy.

clue.text: Capital of India with place to park behind housing

indicators.note: housing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a sofa is where you park your behind, i.e. sit down
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A city in India said to sit behind a car park enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park behind' looks like a parking direction, but it is to park one's behind, i.e. sit: a SOFA, which houses I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Rake in money coming back that expert divides

indicators.note: divides means a piece splits the other in two by sitting inside it

parts.note: a rebate is money returned to you
a pro is an expert, a professional

explanation.surface: A garden rake is bought with cash returned, the purchase split by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man, and a reprobate is an unprincipled person: synonyms.

clue.text: An indefinite number of lines in intersection

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Counting the many lines that meet at a crossing point.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a point where lines or branches meet, a junction.

clue.text: Name that is inspiring work of art?

definitions.text: Name that is inspiring work of art?

parts.note: to call is to name

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Asks for the name of whoever inspires an artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' here means breathing in, i.e. containing. The whole clue also defines: a Muse is one who inspires art.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, one of the goddesses who inspire artists.

clue.text: Drive English leader around in centre of Basildon

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another
centre of picks the two middle letters of the town's name
around turns the pair of pieces back to front

parts.note: PM, Prime Minister, is the country's leader

explanation.surface: An Englishman's leader drives about in the middle of an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the English leader into MPE. Basildon is a town in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to force or urge onward, a synonym of drive.

clue.text: Priest breaking wind instrument in US city

indicators.note: breaking means one piece bursts into the middle of the other

parts.note: a kazoo is a humming instrument you blow into
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman breaks wind loudly somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests breaking wind; 'wind instrument' is one phrase and 'breaking' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in Michigan in the United States.

clue.text: One avoiding consumption that could make nose run

indicators.note: could make means the letters given can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone abstaining from something that gives you a runny nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonuser is a person who does not take a drug or product, so avoids consuming it.

clue.text: Thus, playing D and E flat around piano, it creates effect on one?

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the next piece
playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist plays notes D and E flat softly and wonders about the effect on the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges D EFLAT to FTEDAL, which goes 'around' P. 'One' is a piano, the subject of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft pedal of a piano mutes the sound, producing a quieter effect on the instrument.

clue.text: Not all occupy London's tower

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Protesters occupying a London landmark, though not all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall lattice tower carrying power lines.

clue.text: Respecting boy fencing area in grounds

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the outer letters surround a piece

parts.note: re means regarding or respecting
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: About a lad who puts a fence around a patch in the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' looks like land; it is the definition, as in grounds for a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds for something are the justification for it, its reason.

clue.text: Proof of competence? Officials won't have tons

definitions.note: singular in the clue, but each certificate is one such proof, hence the question mark

indicators.note: won't have means a letter is refused, dropped from the word

parts.note: diplomats are state officials

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats are refusing heavy loads as qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomas are certificates awarded after a course, evidence of qualification.

clue.text: Large number in the Moroccan property I own

parts.note: my means belonging to me, what I own
a riad is a traditional Moroccan house built round a courtyard

explanation.surface: Boasting of the many rooms in one's house in Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: A myriad is a countless multitude, originally ten thousand.

clue.text: Emperor runs a hunting trip that saves time

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: saves means keeps inside, so the trip holds a letter

parts.note: a safari is an expedition to hunt or observe animals

explanation.surface: An emperor dashes off on a hunt that cuts down on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari was the name of Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia, before his coronation.

clue.text: Outside hotel, salesmen knocked back drink

indicators.note: outside means the reversed letters wrap around another piece
knocked back means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen downing drinks outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking; it reverses the salesmen to SPER, which is split to go 'Outside' the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a drink of wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: No need to pay for bed and board in this island

parts.note: an inn supplies lodging and meals
if there is no need to pay, it is free

explanation.surface: A holiday isle where accommodation costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'the INN IS FREE'. Innisfree is famous from Yeats's poem 'The Lake Isle of Innisfree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Innisfree is a small island in Lough Gill, Ireland, immortalised by W. B. Yeats.

clue.text: Spymaster has the leading role in roguery

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
to be chief is to have the leading role

explanation.surface: A spy boss stars in a story about villainy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful misbehaviour or wrongdoing, much like roguery.

clue.text: Some not so awful crimes could be fascinating

indicators.note: not here tells you to remove the following word from the one before
awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess, rearranged

explanation.surface: Remarks that some less dreadful offences might still be gripping to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not so' takes SO from 'Some', leaving ME; 'awful' rearranges CRIMES to SMERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesmeric means hypnotic, gripping attention completely, much as something fascinating does.

clue.text: Girl recalled caress in an ill-advised move

parts.note: a miss is a girl

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pet is to stroke or caress

explanation.surface: A young woman regrets a fondle she remembers as a bad decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep is a blunder, an error of judgement or a false step.

clue.text: Playing well at the moment, do some singing?

definitions.meaning: a player who is ... is performing well currently
to sing is slang for ... to the police

explanation.surface: A performer currently on good form might well break into song.
explanation.definitionFit: In form means playing well, and to inform on someone is to sing to the authorities.

clue.text: Ruminate on a German flower

parts.note: to mull over something is to ruminate on it
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Pondering a German bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullein is a tall plant with spikes of yellow blooms.

clue.text: Perhaps a rhinestone is a national symbol

definitions.meaning: a rhinestone is a fake gem

explanation.surface: A paste gem passed off as the emblem of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, SHAM ROCK, for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock, a three-leaved clover, is Ireland's national emblem; a rhinestone is imitation jewellery.

clue.text: Clever releasing B side

indicators.note: releasing means letting a letter go from the word

parts.note: bright means clever

explanation.surface: A smart record label puts out its flip side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B side' suggests a record's flip; B is the letter released and 'side' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Right is one side, as opposed to left.

clue.text: Carouse as of old, hiding whiskey in mug, say

indicators.note: hiding here means putting a letter out of sight, removing it

parts.note: to wassail is an old word for drinking and making merry
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Old-style revellers stash whisky in their drinking mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a drinking vessel to suit the surface; it is the verb, to rob with violence.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to attack them, one example of the wider verb to assail.

clue.text: It's time to split up gold-plated cube

indicators.note: plated means coated, so the metal surrounds the object

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a small cube used in games

explanation.surface: Time to break up a gilded block.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, said when it is time for people to part.

clue.text: Green skirts hot for nymph

indicators.note: skirts means goes around the edge of something

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green
H abbreviates hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An inexperienced nymph wears steamy skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is the mountain nymph in Greek myth who pined for Narcissus.

clue.text: Eastern dynasty maintains western pronunciation

indicators.note: maintains means holds within, so one piece is inside the other

parts.note: the Tang was a Chinese imperial dynasty

explanation.surface: An Eastern ruling house keeps up a Western accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal accent, a way of saying words.

clue.text: Encroaching characters may be written thus

definitions.meaning: letters can be written ..., joined-up script

explanation.surface: Intrusive letters might be written in this style.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN CURSIVE for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Incursive describes making raids or inroads, intruding on territory.

clue.text: How tennis ace could be described in decisive moment

definitions.text: How tennis ace could be described
definitions.meaning: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return, a point with no return
when one is committed and cannot turn back

explanation.surface: A sports writer describes an unreturnable serve at a crucial juncture.
explanation.definitionFit: The point of no return is the critical stage after which turning back is impossible.
